label: PYQ-style
stem: Give reasons: (i) o-nitrophenol is steam-volatile but p-nitrophenol is not; (ii) Grignard reagents must be prepared under anhydrous conditions.
model_answer:
(i) o-Nitrophenol has *intra*molecular hydrogen bonding, so its molecules are not associated and it is volatile; p-nitrophenol has *inter*molecular hydrogen bonding, so its molecules are associated. [1]
(ii) Grignard reagents react with water (any proton source) to give alkanes: $\ce{RMgX + H2O -> RH + Mg(OH)X}$. [1]

label: PYQ-style
stem: Write the mechanism of the acid-catalysed hydration of ethene to ethanol.
model_answer:
**Step 1** — protonation of the alkene by $\ce{H3O+}$ to form a carbocation:
$\ce{CH2=CH2 + H3O+ -> CH3-CH2+ + H2O}$ [1]
**Step 2** — nucleophilic attack of water on the carbocation:
$\ce{CH3-CH2+ + H2O -> CH3-CH2-OH2+}$ [1]
**Step 3** — deprotonation to give the alcohol:
$\ce{CH3-CH2-OH2+ + H2O -> CH3CH2OH + H3O+}$ [1]

stem:
(a) Write the products of (i) $\ce{(CH3)3C-O-CH3 + HI}$, (ii) $\ce{C6H5-O-CH3 + HI}$. [2]
(b) Why can't tert-butyl methyl ether be made from $\ce{(CH3)3C-Br}$ and $\ce{CH3ONa}$? [1]
model_answer:
(a) (i) $\ce{(CH3)3C-O-CH3 + HI -> (CH3)3C-I + CH3OH}$ (S$_\text{N}$1 through the stable 3$^\circ$ carbocation) [1]
(ii) $\ce{C6H5-O-CH3 + HI -> C6H5OH + CH3I}$ (the O–aryl bond has partial double-bond character and is not broken) [1]
(b) Methoxide is a strong base; with a 3$^\circ$ halide, elimination wins over substitution and 2-methylpropene is formed. The ether is made from $\ce{(CH3)3C-ONa + CH3Br}$ instead. [1]

label: PYQ-style
stem: Compound A ($\ce{C3H8O}$) gives turbidity with Lucas reagent in about five minutes. When vapours of A are passed over copper at 573 K, B ($\ce{C3H6O}$) is formed. Heating A with conc. $\ce{H2SO4}$ at 443 K gives C ($\ce{C3H6}$). C adds HBr to give D, and D gives back A with aqueous KOH. D reacts with sodium in dry ether to give E ($\ce{C6H14}$). Identify A to E and write the equations.
model_answer:
Turbidity in about five minutes ⇒ A is a secondary alcohol.
**A = propan-2-ol**, $\ce{CH3CH(OH)CH3}$   **B = propanone**, $\ce{CH3COCH3}$
**C = propene**, $\ce{CH3CH=CH2}$   **D = 2-bromopropane**, $\ce{CH3CH(Br)CH3}$
**E = 2,3-dimethylbutane**, $\ce{(CH3)2CH-CH(CH3)2}$ [½ each = 2½]
$\ce{CH3CH(OH)CH3 ->[Cu][573 K] CH3COCH3 + H2}$ [½]
$\ce{CH3CH(OH)CH3 ->[conc. H2SO4][443 K] CH3CH=CH2 + H2O}$ [½]
$\ce{CH3CH=CH2 + HBr -> CH3CH(Br)CH3}$ (Markovnikov) [½]
$\ce{CH3CH(Br)CH3 + KOH(aq) -> CH3CH(OH)CH3 + KBr}$ [½]
$\ce{2CH3CH(Br)CH3 + 2Na ->[dry ether] (CH3)2CH-CH(CH3)2 + 2NaBr}$ [½]

label: PYQ-style
stem:
(a) Arrange ethanol, phenol, 4-methylphenol and 4-nitrophenol in increasing order of acid strength and explain the order. [2]
(b) Write equations for what happens when: (i) phenol is heated with zinc dust; (ii) propan-1-ol is oxidised with PCC; (iii) anisole is treated with $\ce{CH3Cl}$ and anhydrous $\ce{AlCl3}$. [3]
model_answer:
(a) ethanol $<$ 4-methylphenol $<$ phenol $<$ 4-nitrophenol [1]
Phenols are more acidic than ethanol because the phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance; ethoxide is not. $\ce{-NO2}$ ($-I$, $-R$) spreads the negative charge further and raises acidity; $\ce{-CH3}$ (+I) intensifies the charge and lowers it. [1]
(b) (i) $\ce{C6H5OH + Zn ->[\Delta] C6H6 + ZnO}$ [1]
(ii) $\ce{CH3CH2CH2OH ->[PCC] CH3CH2CHO}$ (propanal; oxidation stops at the aldehyde) [1]
(iii) $\ce{C6H5OCH3 + CH3Cl ->[anhyd. AlCl3]}$ 4-methoxytoluene (major) + 2-methoxytoluene (minor) + HCl [1]
